Somerville.narrative: Somerville's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with condos leading the charge at a 100% sale-to-list price ratio and a striking 35.7% of units selling above asking price at a median of $922,000 — a clear signal that buyers must come in aggressive with few contingencies to compete. Single-family homes commanded a median of $1,082,500 with 97.9% SP/LP and 25% of sales closing over ask, while multi-families topped the market at $1,360,000 with 18.2% selling above list, reflecting strong investor and owner-occupant demand for income-producing properties. With effectively zero months of supply across all three categories and only 4 single-family homes sold in the past 30 days, inventory is critically thin, creating intense pressure on buyers who face limited choices and bidding wars on nearly every listing. Sellers are in an enviable position right now — properly priced homes in Somerville are moving quickly and often above list, making this an ideal window to maximize returns before any seasonal slowdown.

Cambridge.narrative: Cambridge remains one of Greater Boston's most competitive markets, with condos selling at exactly list price on average and a striking 39.5% of units closing above asking — a clear signal that demand is vastly outpacing supply, which is effectively at zero months. Single families commanded a median of $1,764,000 with 27.3% selling over ask, while multi-families topped the chart at a $2,425,000 median with half of all sales closing above list price. For buyers, the data underscores the need for aggressive, well-prepared offers with minimal contingencies, as hesitation is simply not an option in this inventory-starved environment. Sellers, meanwhile, are in an exceptionally strong position — the near-perfect sale-to-list ratios across all property types suggest that strategic pricing at or near market value will reliably generate multiple offers and competitive escalations.

Milton.narrative: Milton's single-family market is commanding serious attention, with a median sale price of $1,365,000 and 35% of homes selling above asking price at a 98.2% sale-to-list ratio — all against a backdrop of essentially zero months of supply, signaling an intensely undersupplied market. Condos are similarly tight, with a median of $725,000 and a near-perfect 99.7% sale-to-list ratio, though the slim volume of just four sales in the past 30 days underscores how little inventory buyers have to choose from. Multi-family product is scarce as well, with a single sale closing at $1,525,000 and a 98.4% sale-to-list ratio, reflecting strong investor and owner-occupant demand for Milton's coveted two- and three-family stock. For sellers, this is as favorable a landscape as it gets — well-priced homes are moving quickly and near full value — while buyers should expect to act decisively, come in with competitive offers, and anticipate limited negotiating leverage across all property types.

Quincy.narrative: Quincy's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $775,000 and selling at 101.2% of list price — with more than half of all homes, 56.5%, closing above asking. Condos are moving at exactly list price with a $450,000 median, while multi-families are fetching a median of $1,056,000, with 40% of those selling over ask despite a slight dip to 98.9% SP/LP ratio. With 23 single-family and 23 condo sales in the past 30 days and essentially no measurable months of supply reported, inventory is razor-thin across the board, signaling an intensely seller-favored market. Buyers should expect multiple-offer situations and come prepared with strong financials and competitive terms, while sellers are well-positioned to maximize returns — particularly in the single-family segment where bidding wars are the clear norm.

Watertown.narrative: Watertown's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes posting a striking 109.5% sale-to-list ratio and every one of the 2 homes sold in the last 30 days closing above asking price at a median of $1,035,000. The condo market is considerably more active with 18 units traded, a median sale price of $558,000, and nearly 4 in 10 units selling over list — a more accessible entry point but still far from a buyer's market. Multi-families commanded a median of $1,100,000 with 28.6% selling above ask, reflecting strong investor and house-hacker demand in this well-located suburb. With essentially no months of supply across all segments, sellers hold all the cards right now, and buyers should expect to move fast, waive contingencies strategically, and come in well above list price — particularly on single-family homes where overbidding is essentially universal.

Medford.narrative: Medford's real estate market is firing on all cylinders, with single-family homes commanding a median of $1,025,000 and selling at 101.1% of list price — 57% of those closing above asking — while multi-families are even hotter, with 75% selling over ask at a median of $977,500 and a sale-to-list ratio of 102.6%. Condos offer a comparatively accessible entry point at a $688,500 median, though even that segment sees 21% of units trading above list price. With effectively zero months of supply across all property types and 44 combined sales in the past 30 days, inventory is being absorbed as fast as it hits the market, leaving buyers with little room to negotiate and virtually no time to deliberate. Sellers are in an exceptional position right now — particularly multi-family owners — but buyers who come in well-prepared, pre-approved, and aggressive on price stand the best chance of landing a home in this intensely competitive inner-suburb.

Melrose.narrative: Melrose remains an intensely competitive market across all property types, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $918,500 and selling at a remarkable 111.3% of list price — meaning buyers are routinely paying nearly $90,000 or more above asking, with 71.4% of the 14 homes sold in the last 30 days closing over list. Condos offer a comparatively accessible entry point at a $515,000 median, though even that segment sees 60% of units selling above asking at an even 100% SP/LP ratio, signaling strong but slightly less frenzied competition. Multi-family properties are the hottest asset class of all, with the sole sale in the past 30 days closing at $1,110,000 and 111% of list price — and every single multi-family that came to market sold over asking. For sellers, Melrose is about as favorable as it gets, with virtually no supply and buyers waiving contingencies to win; for buyers, expect aggressive competition, pre-inspections, and escalation clauses to be the norm regardless of which property type you're targeting.

Arlington.narrative: Arlington's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes commanding a median of $1,218,000 and selling at virtually full asking price (99.8%), while multi-families are the hottest segment — closing at 104.6% of list price with a striking 75% of sales going over ask at a median of $1,200,000. Condos offer a relative entry point at $877,500, though 30% still sell above list, signaling that no corner of this market is forgiving for buyers. With inventory so tight that months of supply is effectively zero across all categories, sellers hold enormous leverage and can realistically expect multiple offers and near-instant sales regardless of property type. Buyers should arrive pre-approved, prepared to waive contingencies strategically, and ready to move decisively — hesitation in Arlington almost certainly means losing out.

Belmont.narrative: Belmont's real estate market is running at a near-frenzied pace across all property types, with single-family homes posting a median sale price of $1,539,500 and closing at 102.7% of list price — meaning buyers are routinely paying above asking, as evidenced by 62.5% of single-family sales going over ask in the past 30 days. Condos are equally competitive at a $1,015,000 median with 60% selling above list, while the lone multi-family sale hit $1,375,000 at a striking 105.8% of asking price — and every multi-family that came to market sold over ask. With effectively zero months of supply across all categories and only 14 total sales in the past 30 days, inventory is critically thin, giving sellers exceptional pricing power and the confidence to list aggressively. For buyers, Belmont demands pre-emptive offers, waived contingencies, and a willingness to compete hard — this is not a market where patience is rewarded.

Winchester.narrative: Winchester's real estate market is running exceptionally hot across all property types, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $1,775,000 and condos — a segment not typically associated with bidding wars — actually averaging above asking at 100.6% SP/LP, with a remarkable 66.7% of units selling over list price. Single-family inventory is essentially nonexistent, with 11 homes closing in the past 30 days and no measurable months of supply, meaning well-priced listings are being absorbed almost immediately. For buyers, this environment demands pre-approval, decisive offers, and a willingness to compete — particularly on condos, where two-thirds of sellers are receiving multiple bids — while escalation clauses and limited contingencies have become near-standard practice. Sellers, meanwhile, are in an enviable position: with 36.4% of single-family homes closing above asking and virtually no competition on the market, properly staged and priced Winchester properties are generating strong returns with minimal days on market.

Boston.narrative: Boston's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $1,037,500 and a remarkable 41.9% of properties selling above asking price at a full 100% sale-to-list ratio — a clear signal that well-priced homes are sparking bidding wars almost without exception. The condo market, the city's most active segment with 261 sales in the past 30 days, is slightly more measured but still strong, with a $787,000 median and nearly 1 in 5 units selling over ask, while multi-families are leading in raw price at $1,170,000 with 25% of deals exceeding list price. With months of supply effectively at zero across all three categories, inventory is critically constrained, giving sellers extraordinary leverage and the realistic expectation of multiple offers and quick closings. For buyers, this means coming in pre-approved, prepared to waive contingencies strategically, and ready to move fast — hesitation in this market is costly, as homes are not sitting long enough to negotiate from a position of patience.
